## Reflection

Completing CITI training helped me understand why protecting participants must be part of research planning. My main takeaway is the importance of informed consent, voluntary participation, and keeping personal information confidential. These responsibilities matter in marketing research because surveys can collect sensitive information about people's preferences and experiences.

Reviewing CPP's IRB application process also helped me understand that completing training is one step toward conducting research; it does not provide approval for a study. Researchers must determine whether IRB review is needed, prepare their protocol, submit it through Cayuse, and obtain the required approval before recruiting participants or collecting human-subject data. For my research projects, I would apply these principles by explaining the study clearly, collecting only necessary information, and protecting participants' identities.
